questions.question: Accounting information must have some characteristics that will make it useful for the intended users. The characteristic that states that there should be no change in the basis for the preparation of the accounting information from period to period is ______
questions.explanation: Consistency means using the same accounting methods and bases from one period to the next, so users can compare results over time. Strictly, the Conceptual Framework treats consistency as something that supports comparability rather than listing it as a separate characteristic, but it is the only option that describes keeping the same basis each period. Option A is about information being able to influence decisions. Option C is about getting information to users in time to act on it, and option D is about presenting it clearly.

questions.question: The primary objective of the IASB Conceptual Framework is to:

options.b: Provide guidance for developing IFRS Standards

questions.explanation: The Conceptual Framework exists mainly to help the IASB develop IFRS Standards built on consistent concepts, and to help preparers when no standard applies. Option A is wrong because fraud detection is an audit matter. Option C is wrong because tax rules are set by tax law, and option D is wrong because the Framework is not a standard and does not override any standard.

questions.question: According to the Conceptual Framework, the objective of general-purpose financial reporting is to ______

options.a: Provide information useful to investors, lenders, and other creditors

questions.explanation: General-purpose financial reporting aims to give useful information to existing and potential investors, lenders and other creditors for their decisions about providing resources to the entity. Options B and D name users the Framework does not treat as primary users. Option C is too narrow because reports cover the entity's resources, claims and performance, not just management.

questions.question: The fundamental qualitative characteristics of useful financial information are ______ and ______
questions.explanation: Relevance and faithful representation are the two fundamental qualitative characteristics; information must have both to be useful. Options A and B list enhancing characteristics (comparability, verifiability, timeliness, understandability), which add to usefulness but are not fundamental. Option C names neutrality, which is part of faithful representation, and prudence, which supports neutrality.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an enhancing qualitative characteristic of useful financial information?
questions.explanation: Materiality is an entity-specific aspect of relevance, not an enhancing qualitative characteristic. The four enhancing characteristics are comparability, verifiability, timeliness and understandability, so options A, C and D are all on the list.

questions.question: Information is considered relevant if it ______
questions.explanation: Relevant information can make a difference to users' decisions because it has predictive value, confirmatory value or both. Option B describes part of faithful representation. Option C describes comparability, and option D describes understandability, which are enhancing characteristics.

questions.question: Faithful representation requires information to be ______, ______, and ______

options.c: Complete, neutral, and free from error

questions.explanation: To be a faithful representation, information should be complete, neutral and free from error, showing the substance of what it claims to show. Option A lists enhancing characteristics. Option B mixes relevance with materiality, and option D mixes verifiability with consistency, none of which are the three components of faithful representation.

questions.question: An asset is defined as ______ according to the Conceptual Framework

options.a: Any item owned by a company for which cash is paid not bought on credit
options.d: A resource controlled by the entity as a result of past events from which future economic benefits are expected

questions.explanation: An asset is a resource controlled by the entity as a result of past events, from which future economic benefits are expected; control, past events and economic benefits are the main ideas. Option A is wrong because assets bought on credit are still assets. Options B and C are too narrow, because receivables, inventory and intangibles are also assets.

questions.question: According to the IASB framework, a liability is defined as ______

options.a: Any future expense from which liability arises
options.b: A future planned payment arising from credit transactions
options.d: A present obligation arising from past events

questions.explanation: A liability is a present obligation of the entity arising from past events, which is expected to lead to an outflow of economic resources. Options A and B describe future plans or expenses, which create no present obligation. Option C is wrong because owner's equity is the residual interest after deducting liabilities, not a liability.

questions.question: According to the IASB framework, Equity is defined as ______

options.a: Share capital contributed originally by the owners
options.b: Total liabilities arising from past and future credit transactions
options.c: Total assets both bought for cash and on credit
options.d: The residual interest in the assets after deducting liabilities

questions.explanation: Under the IASB Conceptual Framework, equity is the residual interest in the assets of the entity after deducting all its liabilities, so it is simply what is left for the owners. Option A is too narrow because equity also includes retained earnings and reserves, not just the share capital first contributed. Options B and C describe liabilities and assets, which are the two elements used to work out equity, not equity itself.

questions.question: Which of the following is a measurement basis under the Conceptual Framework?
questions.explanation: Historical cost is one of the measurement bases recognised by the Conceptual Framework, alongside current value bases such as fair value, value in use and current cost. Options B and C are wrong because of the word "only" - the Framework does not restrict measurement to a single market or replacement figure. Option D, tax value, is a figure used for tax purposes and is not a measurement basis in the Framework.

questions.question: A business is a going concern with no intentions to reduce or curtail its operations. Which would be the most relevant valuation for its machinery - the net realisable value of the machinery or its depreciated cost?

options.a: Net realisable value, because the machinery could be sold at any time
options.b: Depreciated cost, because the business will continue to use the machinery rather than sell it
options.c: Scrap value, because it is the most prudent figure
options.d: Original cost with no depreciation, because the machinery is still in use

questions.explanation: For a going concern the machinery is expected to be used in the business, not sold, so its depreciated cost is the most relevant value. Option A would only be more relevant if the business were not a going concern and the assets were likely to be sold. Option C undervalues an asset that is still earning money, and option D ignores the fact that the machinery wears out over time.

questions.question: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) vary from country to country mainly because

options.a: the legal and regulatory systems of countries are not the same
options.b: the IASB issues a different set of standards for each country
options.c: each country uses a different reporting currency
options.d: companies in different countries differ in size

questions.explanation: GAAP differ across countries because each country has its own legal and regulatory system, and those rules shape local accounting practice. Option C is wrong because currency does not change the principles applied, and option B is wrong because the IASB issues one uniform set of IFRS for worldwide use.

questions.question: Common sets of principles and procedures that define the basis of financial accounting policies and practices are known as
questions.explanation: Accounting standards are the common principles and procedures on which an entity's accounting policies and practices are based, covering assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses and equity. Option D is only a proposed standard issued for comment, and option C refers to the broad classes such as assets and income, not to rules of practice.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the legal status of accounting standards is correct?

options.a: They are binding only on the members of the IASB
options.b: They apply only to companies listed on a stock exchange in the United Kingdom
options.c: They automatically become law in every country once issued by the IASB
options.d: They do not have the force of law but become effective when a country adopts them

questions.explanation: Accounting standards are not law by themselves; they become effective in a country only when that country adopts them, as Nigeria did for listed companies. Option C is wrong because IASB pronouncements have no automatic legal force, and option A is wrong because the standards are meant for entities, not for the Board members who write them.

questions.question: Accounting standards apply to

options.a: only the revenue and expenses of an entity
options.b: only the statement of financial position of listed companies
options.c: the whole spectrum of an entity's transactions and events, including assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses and equity

questions.explanation: Accounting standards cover all of an entity's financial transactions and other events, so assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses and equity all fall within them. Options A and D are too narrow, and option B wrongly limits them to one statement and one type of company.

questions.question: The body responsible for issuing new International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRSs) is the
questions.explanation: The IASB, often called the Board, issues new IFRSs and has full responsibility for all technical matters. Option D, the FRCN, is the Nigerian body through which compliance with IFRS is ensured locally, but it does not issue IFRSs, and option A is a stock exchange, not a standard setter.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the documents issued by the IASB?

options.a: Final interpretations of the IFRS Interpretations Committee
options.b: Revised International Accounting Standards and IFRSs
options.d: Audited financial statements of listed companies

questions.explanation: Audited financial statements are prepared by companies and audited by their auditors; the IASB does not issue them. Options C, B and A are all genuine IASB outputs: exposure drafts, revised IASs and IFRSs, and final IFRS Interpretations Committee interpretations.

questions.question: Which of the following is a responsibility of the IASB?

options.a: Preparing the annual financial statements of listed companies
options.b: Issuing the Conceptual Framework that sets out the concepts underlying financial statements
options.c: Deciding how much tax companies should pay
options.d: Auditing the financial statements of multinational companies

questions.explanation: The IASB issues the Conceptual Framework, which sets out the concepts behind the preparation and presentation of financial statements, as well as the IFRSs themselves. Option A is the job of each company's management, option D is done by external auditors, and option C is a government function.

questions.question: A coherent system of interrelated objectives and fundamental concepts that prescribes the nature, function and limits of financial accounting and reporting is called
questions.explanation: This is the definition of the Conceptual Framework: a coherent system of objectives and concepts that guides consistent standard-setting. Option A is an individual standard dealing with specific transactions, and option C is the country-specific body of accounting rules and practices, not a system of fundamental concepts.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a stated purpose of the Conceptual Framework?

options.a: To assist entities in developing consistent accounting policies when no Standard applies
options.b: To assess how efficiently management has used the entity's resources
options.c: To assist all stakeholders to understand and interpret IFRS Accounting Standards
options.d: To assist the IASB in developing and revising IFRS Accounting Standards

questions.explanation: Assessing how efficiently management has used resources is stewardship, something users do with financial reports, not a purpose of the Conceptual Framework. Options D, A and C are the three stated purposes: helping the IASB set standards, helping entities develop policies, and helping stakeholders interpret the standards.

questions.question: Ikeja Agro Ltd enters into a new type of transaction for which no IFRS Accounting Standard applies. To develop a consistent accounting policy for it, the company should look to

options.a: whatever treatment gives the highest profit
options.b: the listing rules of the Nigerian Exchange Group

questions.explanation: One purpose of the Conceptual Framework is to help entities develop consistent accounting policies when no IFRS Accounting Standard applies to a transaction. Option D is a tax document, not a basis for accounting policy, and option A would break the neutrality that faithful representation requires.

questions.question: Apart from cases where no Standard applies, the Conceptual Framework also assists entities in developing accounting policies when

options.a: a Standard allows a choice of accounting policy
options.c: the entity is not a going concern
options.d: the entity wants to reduce its tax liability

questions.explanation: The Conceptual Framework helps entities choose consistent policies both when no Standard applies and when a Standard allows a choice of accounting policy. Options D and B are not situations the Framework is designed for, and option C has nothing to do with this purpose.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT set out in the 2018 revised Conceptual Framework?

options.a: Concepts relating to capital and capital maintenance
options.b: Rates for computing company income tax
options.c: The qualitative characteristics of useful financial information
options.d: The objective of general purpose financial reporting

questions.explanation: Tax rates are set by tax law, not by the Conceptual Framework. Options D, C and A are all part of its scope, along with the reporting entity, the elements, recognition and derecognition, measurement bases, and presentation and disclosure.

questions.question: Which of the following is included in the scope of the 2018 revised Conceptual Framework?

options.b: Measurement bases and guidance on when to use them
options.d: Detailed audit procedures for testing inventory

questions.explanation: The 2018 Conceptual Framework includes measurement bases and guidance on when to use them. Options D, C and A are matters for auditing standards, company law and stock exchange rules, not the Conceptual Framework.

questions.question: In the Conceptual Framework, the criteria for including assets and liabilities in financial statements and the guidance on when to remove them are referred to respectively as
questions.explanation: Recognition is about including assets and liabilities in the financial statements, while derecognition is about removing them. Option B reverses the two terms, and option C deals with how amounts are valued and explained, not whether items are included.

questions.question: Within the scope of the Conceptual Framework, guidance on the 'reporting entity' deals with

options.a: measurement bases and when to use them
options.b: a description of the reporting entity and its boundary
options.d: the definitions of income and expenses

questions.explanation: The reporting entity part of the Conceptual Framework describes the reporting entity and its boundary. Options D, C and A are separate items in the scope, dealing with the elements, capital maintenance and measurement.

questions.question: The benefit of the Conceptual Framework that comes from providing a common set of principles, making it easier to compare financial statements across companies and periods, is
questions.explanation: Consistency and comparability arises because a common set of principles leads to similar accounting practices, so statements can be compared across companies and over time. Option C is about helping the IASB develop standards, and option B is about helping companies develop accounting policies.

questions.question: The benefit of the Conceptual Framework that provides guidance to companies in developing accounting policies, especially when specific standards are not available, is
questions.explanation: Preparers are the companies that produce financial statements, so guidance for them in developing accounting policies is the assistance to preparers benefit. Option B refers to the IASB and other standard setters, and option A refers to investors, lenders and analysts understanding the statements.

questions.question: The benefit of the Conceptual Framework that helps investors, lenders and analysts to better understand and interpret financial statements is
questions.explanation: Enhanced understanding is the benefit to all stakeholders, such as investors, lenders and analysts, in interpreting financial statements. Option B is aimed at the companies preparing the statements, and option D is aimed at the IASB and other standard setters.

questions.question: Financial statements intended to meet the information needs common to users who are unable to command the preparation of reports tailored to their own needs are called
questions.explanation: General purpose financial reports serve the common needs of users who cannot demand reports made specially for them. Option D is the opposite, being prepared for a particular user or group, and option C is internal reporting for managers.

questions.question: First Lagoon Bank asks Kano Textiles Ltd to prepare a report in a format designed only for the bank's loan assessment. Such a report is best described as
questions.explanation: A special-purpose financial statement is prepared to meet the demands of a particular user or group of users, as here for one bank. Option C is wrong because general purpose reports serve the common needs of many users who cannot ask for tailored reports, and option D is a draft standard issued by the IASB.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about general purpose financial reports (GPFR) is correct?

options.a: GPFR cannot provide all the information users need, so users also consider information from other sources
options.b: GPFR need not comply with accounting standards
options.c: GPFR provide all the information users need to make economic decisions
options.d: GPFR are prepared mainly to meet the needs of a particular user

questions.explanation: General purpose financial reports cannot provide all the information users need, so users must also consider pertinent information from other sources. Option D describes special-purpose statements, and option B is wrong because GPFR comply with accounting standards and GAAP.

questions.question: The primary users of general purpose financial reports are

options.a: managers and employees of the entity
options.c: present and potential investors, lenders and other creditors

questions.explanation: The primary users are present and potential investors, lenders and other creditors, because they cannot demand tailored information yet must make decisions about the entity. Options B, A and D may find GPFR useful but are not regarded as primary users.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primary user of general purpose financial reports?

options.a: A potential investor considering buying shares
options.b: A bank that has lent money to the entity
options.c: A present shareholder of the entity
options.d: The government deciding how much tax to collect

questions.explanation: The government is listed among the other users who may find GPFR useful, but it is not a primary user. Options C and A are present and potential investors, and option B is a lender, all of whom are primary users.

questions.question: Prudential and market regulators such as the Central Bank of Nigeria are best described, in relation to general purpose financial reports, as

options.b: primary users to whom GPFR are mainly directed
options.c: the only users entitled to receive GPFR
options.d: other users who may find GPFR useful but are not primary users

questions.explanation: Regulators are classed as other users: they may find GPFR useful, but the reports are not primarily directed to them. Option B is wrong because the primary users are investors, lenders and other creditors, and option A is wrong because GPFR are prepared by the entity itself.

questions.question: When primary users assess how effectively and efficiently management has discharged its responsibilities to use the entity's resources, they are assessing
questions.explanation: Stewardship is how well management has looked after and used the entity's resources, and primary users need information to assess it. Option C is an aspect of relevance, option B is an enhancing qualitative characteristic, and option D is about whether the business will continue operating.

questions.question: Primary users need information about the resources of an entity to assess

options.a: the amount of tax payable by the entity
options.b: the quality of the entity's products
options.c: the entity's prospects for future net cash inflows
options.d: the personal wealth of the directors

questions.explanation: Primary users need information to assess the entity's prospects for future net cash inflows and management's stewardship of resources. Option B is the interest of customers, and option A is the interest of the government.

questions.question: Primary users use financial information to make decisions about all of the following EXCEPT

options.a: buying, selling or holding equity or debt instruments
options.b: judging the quality of the entity's products before buying them
options.c: providing or settling loans and other forms of credit
options.d: exercising rights to vote on management's actions

questions.explanation: Judging product quality is the concern of customers, who are not primary users. Options A, C and D are exactly the decisions investors, lenders and other creditors make with GPFR.

questions.question: Trade creditors (payables) of a business are mainly interested in its
questions.explanation: Trade creditors want to know whether the business can pay what it owes them as debts fall due, which is liquidity. Option C is the customers' concern, option B is the government's, and option A is management's.

questions.question: Which user group is interested in the profitability of a business for tax purposes and policy formulation?
questions.explanation: The government looks at profitability to decide tax and to formulate policy. Option A cares about product quality, option D about liquidity, and option B about liquidity, profitability and survival for job security.

questions.question: Customers of a business are mainly interested in

options.a: the quality of its products or services
options.b: appraisal of the efficiency of management performance

questions.explanation: Customers are interested in the quality of the products or services they buy. Option D is the interest of trade creditors, option B is the interest of owners and investors, and option C is the interest of government.

questions.question: Which user group is interested in information that permits appraisal of the efficiency of management performance?
questions.explanation: Owners and investors entrust their money to management, so they want information to appraise how efficiently management is performing. Option B cares about product quality, option A about liquidity, and option D about profitability for tax and policy.

questions.question: The workers' union of a Lagos manufacturing company studies its financial statements to judge whether jobs and wages are secure. The information this group is interested in is the business's
questions.explanation: Employees are interested in liquidity, profitability and survival, because these determine whether wages will be paid and jobs will last. Option B is the customers' interest, option A is the government's, and option C is the interest of financial analysts.

questions.question: Which user group is interested in the overall performance, growth and survival of the business?
questions.explanation: Management, who guide the company, are interested in its overall performance, growth and survival. Option C focuses on product quality, option B on liquidity, and option A on profitability for tax and policy.

questions.question: Financial analysts are interested in information that permits

options.a: appraisal of the entire business activities
options.d: confirmation of employees' job security only

questions.explanation: Financial analysts want information that permits an appraisal of the entire business activities, so they can advise others. Option B is the customers' focus, option C the government's, and option D is narrower than what analysts look at.

questions.question: Lenders to a business are interested in its

options.c: liquidity, profitability and the reliability of its assets

questions.explanation: Lenders want to know that the business can pay interest and repay the loan, so they look at liquidity, profitability and the reliability of the business assets that may secure the loan. Option D is the customers' concern, and option B is the government's.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an enhancing qualitative characteristic?
questions.explanation: Relevance is a fundamental qualitative characteristic, not an enhancing one. Comparability, verifiability, timeliness and understandability are the enhancing characteristics, so options B, D and A are all genuine enhancing characteristics.

questions.question: Which of the following is an enhancing qualitative characteristic?
questions.explanation: Understandability is one of the four enhancing characteristics, together with comparability, verifiability and timeliness. Option D is an aspect of relevance, while options B and A are underlying features of faithful representation.

questions.question: Accounting information that has the ability to influence users' decisions and can be used for prediction and confirmatory purposes is said to have
questions.explanation: Relevance is the ability of information to make a difference to decisions, through predictive value and confirmatory value. Option B is about depicting the substance of what happened completely, neutrally and without error, and option C is about independent observers reaching consensus.

questions.question: Materiality is an entity-specific aspect of
questions.explanation: Materiality is an entity-specific aspect of relevance: it is judged by the nature or size of an item in the context of the individual entity's report. Option C is the other fundamental characteristic, while options A and D are enhancing characteristics.

questions.question: Materiality is judged on the basis of

options.a: the legal form of the transaction only
options.b: a fixed percentage of profit set by the IASB for all entities
options.c: the nature or magnitude (or both) of the item in the context of the individual entity
options.d: whether the item has been audited

questions.explanation: Materiality depends on the nature or size (or both) of an item in the context of the particular entity's report. Option B is wrong because materiality is entity-specific, not a uniform threshold, and option A confuses it with the idea of legal form.

questions.question: An omission of N2 million would seriously mislead the users of a small Yaba printing business, but would be trivial in the accounts of a large commercial bank. This shows that materiality is

options.b: a uniform amount fixed for all entities

questions.explanation: The same amount can matter greatly to one entity and hardly at all to another, because materiality is an entity-specific aspect of relevance. Option B contradicts the scenario, and option A is wrong because materiality belongs under relevance, a fundamental characteristic.

questions.question: Faithful representation means representing

options.a: information early enough to influence decisions
options.b: the legal form of a transaction regardless of its substance
options.c: the substance of an economic phenomenon instead of its legal form only
options.d: only those transactions that are supported by a written contract

questions.explanation: Faithful representation requires reporting the economic substance of a transaction, not just its legal form. Option B is the reverse of this, and option A describes timeliness, an enhancing characteristic.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an underlying characteristic of faithful representation?
questions.explanation: Timeliness is an enhancing qualitative characteristic about information arriving early enough to be used. Options C, A and B are the three underlying characteristics that faithful representation seeks to maximise.

questions.question: The managing director of Oshodi Foods Ltd chooses estimates that are deliberately slanted to make the company's results look more favourable to investors. The financial statements lack
questions.explanation: Neutrality means information is not biased or slanted to influence users in a particular direction, so deliberately favourable estimates violate it. Option A is about including all necessary information, option D is about when information is available, and option B is about comparing across entities and periods.

questions.question: Aba Plastics Ltd leaves out of its financial statements all information about a large bank loan it took during the year. Which underlying characteristic of faithful representation is most clearly missing?
questions.explanation: A complete depiction includes all the information users need, so omitting a large loan makes the statements incomplete. Option D is about freedom from bias rather than missing items, and options C and B are enhancing characteristics, not underlying features of faithful representation.

questions.question: If a business is NOT a going concern, the more relevant valuation for its machinery would be
questions.explanation: When a business is not a going concern, its assets are expected to be sold, so net realisable value becomes more relevant to users. Option A is the relevant value only when the business will continue, and option B ignores depreciation and the expected sale.

questions.question: A business that is expected to continue operating into the future, with no intention or need to liquidate or curtail its operations, is described as
questions.explanation: A going concern is a business that will continue into the foreseeable future, which is why its assets can be valued on the assumption that they will be used rather than sold. Option B is any entity that prepares financial statements, whether or not it will continue, and option A is a type of liability.

questions.question: An investor examines the trend in sales revenue of Ogun Cement Plc over the past five years and compares its performance with two similar cement companies. The investor is relying mainly on
questions.explanation: Comparability lets users identify changes in a business over time, such as a five-year sales trend, and evaluate it against similar businesses. Option C is about information arriving in time, option D is about independent observers reaching consensus, and option A is an aspect of relevance.

questions.question: Understandability assumes that users of financial reports

options.a: have a reasonable knowledge of business and economic activities and review the information diligently
options.c: can demand tailored reports from the entity
options.d: have no knowledge of business and need everything simplified

questions.explanation: Understandability assumes users have a reasonable knowledge of business and economic activities and will review and analyse the information diligently. Option D wrongly assumes no knowledge, and option C describes users of special-purpose reports.

questions.question: Information that is made available early enough for its use and is still capable of influencing users' decisions has the quality of
questions.explanation: Timeliness means having information available to decision-makers in time to influence their decisions. Option A is about comparing over time and across businesses, option D is about independent observers reaching consensus, and option C is about freedom from bias.

questions.question: When different knowledgeable and independent observers could reach consensus that a particular depiction is a faithful representation, the information is said to be
questions.explanation: Verifiability means independent, knowledgeable observers could agree that the depiction is a faithful representation. Option D is about availability in time, option A is about comparing across periods and businesses, and option C is about whether an item could influence decisions.

questions.question: For information to be verifiable, knowledgeable and independent observers must be able to reach

options.b: consensus, although not necessarily complete agreement
options.c: agreement with the views of management
options.d: the same figure as the tax authorities

questions.explanation: Verifiability requires only consensus among knowledgeable, independent observers, not complete agreement. Option A sets a stricter standard than the definition, and option C is wrong because the observers must be independent, not simply follow management.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about a reporting entity is correct?

options.a: It must always be a single legal entity
options.b: It cannot be a portion of an entity
options.c: It is not necessarily a legal entity
options.d: It must be listed on a stock exchange

questions.explanation: A reporting entity is any entity that is required, or chooses, to prepare financial statements, and it need not be a legal entity. Option A is wrong because it can be a portion of an entity or more than one entity, and option B directly contradicts the definition.

questions.question: An entity that is required, or chooses, to prepare financial statements is known as
questions.explanation: A reporting entity is one that is required, or chooses, to prepare financial statements. Option A describes a business expected to continue operating, option B is an investor, lender or other creditor who uses the statements, and option D is a body such as the IASB.

questions.question: Delta Holdings Plc and its three subsidiaries prepare one set of financial statements covering all four companies together. Which statement about this reporting entity is correct?

options.a: A reporting entity can comprise more than one entity
options.b: This is not allowed because a reporting entity must be a single legal entity
options.c: Each subsidiary must stop preparing records
options.d: Only Delta Holdings Plc can be a reporting entity

questions.explanation: A reporting entity can be a single entity, a portion of an entity, or more than one entity, so a group reporting together is acceptable. Options B and D wrongly assume a reporting entity must be one legal entity, and option C has no basis in the definition.

questions.question: The broad classes into which the financial effects of transactions and other events are grouped according to their economic characteristics are called
questions.explanation: Financial statements group transactions into broad classes by economic characteristics, and these classes are the elements: assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses. Option C describes what makes information useful, and option B is about how amounts are measured.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an element directly related to the statement of financial position?
questions.explanation: Income is an element related to performance, reported in the statement of profit or loss. Options B, A and C are the three elements directly related to the statement of financial position.

questions.question: The elements of financial statements directly related to the measurement of performance are
questions.explanation: Performance is measured by income and expenses, which are reported in the statement of profit or loss. Options C, D and A are combinations of the financial position elements.

questions.question: The statement of cash flows reflects

options.a: none of the elements of financial statements
options.d: both income statement elements and some changes in statement of financial position elements

questions.explanation: The statement of cash flows draws on both performance elements and some changes in financial position elements. Options C and B each leave out one side, and option A is wrong because the statement is linked to the elements.

questions.question: A resource controlled by the entity as a result of past events and from which future economic benefits are expected to flow to the entity is
questions.explanation: This is the definition of an asset: control, a past event and expected future economic benefits. Option B is a present obligation leading to an outflow, option C is the residual interest after deducting liabilities, and option A is an increase in economic benefits during the period.

questions.question: In the definition of an asset, 'control' means

options.b: the ability to obtain the economic benefits and to restrict the access of others
options.c: the right to sell the item at any time without restriction
options.d: legal ownership evidenced by a title document

questions.explanation: Control is the ability to obtain the economic benefits from a resource and to restrict others from getting them, for example by being the sole user of plant and machinery. Option D confuses control with legal form, and option A is wrong because physical possession alone does not give control of the benefits.

questions.question: A present obligation of the entity arising from past events, the settlement of which is expected to result in an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits, is
questions.explanation: This is the definition of a liability: a present obligation from a past event that is expected to lead to an outflow of resources. Option A brings in benefits rather than taking them out, and option B is a decrease in equity during the period rather than an obligation.

questions.question: An obligation that results from an entity's expected practice rather than being required by law or a legal contract is called
questions.explanation: A constructive obligation arises from an entity's established practice or published policy, not from law or contract. Option D is the opposite, being required by law or contract, and option C relates to owners' capital, not to obligations.

questions.question: Niger Delta Oil Ltd has a published policy of cleaning up any environmental damage it causes, even though no law requires it. The obligation to clean up damage already caused is
questions.explanation: Because the obligation comes from the company's published environmental policy rather than legislation, it is a constructive obligation. Option C is wrong because no law requires the clean-up, and option B is wrong because an obligation can be constructive as well as legal.

questions.question: At its reporting date of 31 December, Lekki Logistics Ltd has only discussed a five-year lease that it plans to sign in March of the following year. Why is no liability recognised for this lease at 31 December?

options.b: The lessor is not a primary user
options.d: The past event giving rise to the obligation has not yet happened

questions.explanation: A liability must arise from a past event, so a lease contract must have been signed before the reporting date to create an obligation. Option C is wrong because signed leases can create liabilities, and option A is not the issue in the scenario.

questions.question: The residual interest in the assets of an entity after deducting all its liabilities is
questions.explanation: Equity is what is left for the owners once all liabilities are deducted from assets, so Equity = Assets - Liabilities. Option A is an increase in economic benefits during a period, and option D is a valuation basis for assets.

questions.question: An increase in economic benefits during the accounting period, in the form of inflows or enhancements of assets or decreases of liabilities that increase equity, other than contributions from equity participants, is
questions.explanation: This is the definition of income, which covers both revenue and gains but excludes contributions from owners. Option D is a resource controlled by the entity, not an increase during a period, and option C is the residual interest itself rather than an increase in it.

questions.question: The shareholders of Ibadan Bakeries Ltd pay N5 million in cash for new shares. How is this treated under the definitions of the elements?

options.a: It is revenue because it arises from ordinary activities
options.b: It is a liability because the shareholders own the company
options.c: It is income because cash has increased
options.d: It increases equity but is not income, because it is a contribution from equity participants

questions.explanation: Income excludes increases in equity that come from contributions by equity participants, so a share issue increases equity without being income. Option C ignores this exclusion, and option A is wrong because issuing shares is not part of selling bread.

questions.question: Ibadan Bakeries Ltd pays a cash dividend of N1.5 million to its shareholders. Under the definitions of the elements, the dividend is

options.a: not an expense, because it is a distribution to equity participants
options.b: a loss, because no goods were received
options.d: an expense, because cash has decreased

questions.explanation: Expenses exclude decreases in equity that relate to distributions to equity participants, so a dividend reduces equity but is not an expense. Option D ignores this exclusion, and option B is wrong because losses are a type of expense and the same exclusion applies.

questions.question: The definition of income in the Framework encompasses
questions.explanation: Income covers both revenue from ordinary activities and gains, which may or may not arise from ordinary activities. Options B and C each leave out one part, and option D is wrong because contributions from owners are excluded from income.

questions.question: Gains are not regarded as a separate element in the Framework because

options.a: they always arise outside the ordinary activities of the entity
options.b: they represent increases in economic benefits and are no different in nature from revenue
options.c: they are contributions from equity participants
options.d: they are reported only in the statement of financial position

questions.explanation: Gains are increases in economic benefits, just like revenue, so they are part of the income element rather than a separate element. Option A is wrong because gains may or may not arise from ordinary activities, and option C is wrong because owner contributions are excluded from income altogether.

questions.question: Revenue arises in the course of an entity's ordinary activities and is referred to by different names. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: Revenue goes by names such as sales, fees, interest, dividends, royalties and rent. Capital contributed by owners is a contribution from equity participants and is excluded from income, so it is not revenue, while options C, B and A are all names for revenue.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an expense arising in the course of the ordinary activities of an entity?

options.b: Repayment of a bank loan's principal

questions.explanation: Wages, like cost of sales and depreciation, are ordinary expenses that reduce equity. Option A is a distribution to equity participants, option B reduces a liability and an asset equally without reducing equity, and option C swaps one asset for another.

questions.question: Losses are not treated as a separate element of financial statements because

options.a: they always arise from the ordinary activities of the entity
options.b: they are decreases in economic benefits and are no different in nature from other expenses
options.d: they are distributions to equity participants

questions.explanation: Losses are decreases in economic benefits, just like other expenses, so they fall under the expense element. Option A is wrong because losses may or may not arise from ordinary activities, and option C is wrong because losses do reduce equity.

questions.question: Yaba Tech Solutions Ltd has total assets of N85m and total liabilities of N32m. What is its equity?
questions.explanation: Equity is the residual interest in assets after deducting liabilities, so N85m - N32m = N53m. Option A wrongly adds liabilities to assets, while options D and C simply repeat the asset or liability total.

questions.question: Surulere Stores has equity of N40m and liabilities of N25m. Using the accounting equation, its total assets are
questions.explanation: Assets = Equity + Liabilities, so N40m + N25m = N65m. Option A wrongly subtracts liabilities from equity, and options D and B each leave out one side of the equation.

questions.question: Kaduna Farms Ltd reports total assets of N120m and equity of N70m. What are its total liabilities?
questions.explanation: Since Assets = Equity + Liabilities, Liabilities = Assets - Equity = N120m - N70m = N50m. Option B adds the two figures, and options D and C just repeat one of the given amounts.

questions.question: Ota Furniture Ltd has assets of N50m and liabilities of N20m. It then buys equipment for N5m on credit. What is its equity after the purchase?
questions.explanation: Buying on credit increases assets and liabilities by the same N5m, so equity stays at N50m - N20m = N30m. Option D wrongly treats the purchase as an expense, option B wrongly treats it as income, and option C is the new asset total, not equity.

questions.question: Abeokuta Motors Ltd has assets of N60m and liabilities of N25m. It repays N4m of a bank loan in cash. What are its total liabilities after the repayment?
questions.explanation: Repaying a loan reduces cash (an asset) and the loan (a liability) by N4m, so liabilities fall to N25m - N4m = N21m. Option B ignores the repayment, option C adds it instead of subtracting, and option D is the equity figure, which is unchanged at N35m.

questions.question: Ilorin Traders Ltd had equity of N30m at the start of the year and N48m at the end. During the year shareholders contributed N10m of new capital and N4m of dividends were paid. What was the profit (income less expenses) for the year?
questions.explanation: Equity changes through profit, owner contributions and distributions, so profit = N48m - N30m - N10m + N4m = N12m. Option D ignores both owner transactions, option B removes the contribution but forgets to add back the dividends, and option C reverses both adjustments.

questions.question: In its first month, Enugu Prints Ltd received N8m capital from its owners, earned N3m revenue in cash, paid wages of N1.2m and paid a dividend of N0.5m. What is its total income for the month?
questions.explanation: Income excludes contributions from equity participants, so only the N3m revenue counts as income. Option A wrongly includes the owners' capital, while options C and D deduct wages and dividends, which gives a net figure rather than income.

questions.question: Using the same data (owners' capital N8m, cash revenue N3m, wages N1.2m, dividend N0.5m), what are Enugu Prints Ltd's total expenses for the month?
questions.explanation: Expenses exclude distributions to equity participants, so only the wages of N1.2m are an expense. Option C wrongly adds the dividend, option D counts only the dividend, and option A is profit, not expenses.

questions.question: Using the same data (owners' capital N8m, cash revenue N3m, wages N1.2m, dividend N0.5m) and starting from zero, what is Enugu Prints Ltd's equity at the end of the month?
questions.explanation: Equity rises by the owners' capital and the profit and falls by the dividend: N8m + (N3m - N1.2m) - N0.5m = N9.3m. Option B is profit alone, option C forgets the dividend, and option D ignores both wages and dividend.

questions.question: IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers was issued in ______
questions.explanation: IFRS 15 was issued by the IASB in May 2014, replacing older revenue standards such as IAS 18 and IAS 11. Option B is the date the standard became effective, not when it was issued. Option C is when the revised Conceptual Framework was published, and option A relates to the revised IAS 1.

questions.question: Revenue is to be recognised by a vendor when ______ over the goods or services is transferred to the customer.
questions.explanation: Under IFRS 15, revenue is recognised when (or as) control of the promised goods or services passes to the customer, meaning the customer can direct their use and obtain substantially all the remaining benefits. Options B and D are only indicators that control may have passed; they are not the test itself. Option A reflects the old risks-and-rewards idea, which IFRS 15 replaced with the control model.

questions.question: ______ is an agreement between two or more parties that creates enforceable rights and obligations.
questions.explanation: IFRS 15 defines a contract as an agreement between two or more parties that creates enforceable rights and obligations, and identifying it is step one of the five-step model. Option B is a promise inside a contract to transfer a good or service. Option D is the consideration expected, and option C is one of the parties, not the agreement itself.

questions.question: A party that has contracted with an entity to obtain goods or services that are an output of the entity's ordinary activities in exchange for consideration is generally referred to as ______
questions.explanation: This is the IFRS 15 definition of a customer: someone who contracts to obtain the entity's ordinary outputs in exchange for consideration. Option C provides goods to the entity rather than buying from it. Option B is someone the entity owes money to, and option D obtains the right to use an asset under a lease, which falls under a different standard.

questions.question: A software company sells a bundle that includes both a software licence and a 12-month support service for a total price of N1,300,000. If sold separately, the software licence would sell for N1,100,000 and the support service N600,000. Allocating the transaction price on the basis of relative stand-alone selling prices, how much is allocated to the software licence and the support service?
questions.explanation: The total stand-alone selling price is N1,100,000 + N600,000 = N1,700,000, so the licence gets 1,100,000/1,700,000 x N1,300,000 = N841,176 and the support gets 600,000/1,700,000 x N1,300,000 = N458,824 (together N1,300,000). Option B puts the whole N400,000 discount on the support service, and option D puts it all on the licence. Option A splits the price equally, ignoring the stand-alone selling prices.

questions.question: The effective date for IFRS 15 was ______
questions.explanation: IFRS 15 applies to annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2018. Option D is when the standard was issued, not when it took effect. Option C is linked to the revised IAS 1, and option B is linked to the 2018 Conceptual Framework amendments.

questions.question: A ______ is a promise in a contract to transfer to the customer a good or service that is distinct from other goods or services in the contract.
questions.explanation: A performance obligation is a promise to transfer a distinct good or service, and identifying these is step two of the IFRS 15 five-step model. Option B is the consideration the entity expects to receive. Option C is what an item would sell for on its own, used to allocate the price, and option D is a right to consideration for work already done.

questions.question: Coy ABC has a customer, Coy XYZ, which is undergoing restructuring due to issues relating to liquidity. Coy ABC has decided not to do any further business with Coy XYZ. In response, Coy XYZ informed Coy ABC that it would get a letter of credit from a nationalised bank against which Coy ABC can dispatch goods worth $15,000. Coy ABC has already manufactured the goods exclusively for Coy XYZ, but the letter of credit has not yet been finalised. When should Coy ABC recognise the revenue?

options.a: Not until the letter of credit is finalised (so payment becomes probable) and the goods are transferred to Coy XYZ
options.b: Immediately, because the goods have already been manufactured exclusively for Coy XYZ
options.c: As soon as Coy XYZ says it will obtain a letter of credit
options.d: Never, because Coy XYZ is undergoing restructuring

questions.explanation: Under IFRS 15 a contract only exists for revenue purposes if it is probable that the entity will collect the consideration, so Coy ABC must wait until the letter of credit is finalised and then recognise revenue when control of the goods passes to Coy XYZ. Option B is wrong because making the goods does not transfer control or prove collectability. Option C is wrong because a promise to get a letter of credit is not yet security for payment, and option D is wrong because the contract can still qualify later once the criteria are met.

questions.question: On 1 April 2024, BigBoss Ltd agrees to sell 1,000 Endoscopy Machines to SmallBoss Ltd, which are produced using a pre-fabricated tool supplied by another vendor. The payment terms between BigBoss Ltd and SmallBoss Ltd have not been decided as they are dependent on the price of the pre-fabricated tool, which is yet to be finalised. BigBoss Ltd was paid a non-refundable amount of $4,500. How should BigBoss Ltd account for this transaction under IFRS 15 if BigBoss was the principal in this transaction?

options.a: Recognise the $4,500 as revenue immediately because it is non-refundable
options.b: Recognise revenue for all 1,000 machines on 1 April 2024
options.c: Record the $4,500 as a liability until the IFRS 15 contract criteria are met

questions.explanation: Because the payment terms have not been identified, the arrangement does not yet meet the IFRS 15 criteria for a contract with a customer, so the $4,500 received is held as a liability until those criteria are met. Option A is tempting because the money cannot be refunded, but non-refundable cash alone does not make it revenue while the contract is incomplete. Option B is wrong because no machines have been transferred, and option D is wrong because a customer payment is never equity.

questions.question: ABC Limited enters a contract with a customer to supply a licence for a standard software product. ABC Limited will also install the software, provide updates to the software and technical support for five years. ABC Limited sees the licence and technical support separately; the software will continue to operate without the software updates, and ABC Limited sub-contracts the installation of the software to several approved installers throughout the country. Identify the distinct goods or services (performance obligations).

options.a: One: the whole bundle is a single performance obligation
options.b: Two: the software licence and technical support only
options.c: Three: the software licence, software updates and technical support only
options.d: Four: the software licence, installation service, software updates and technical support

questions.explanation: Each promise is distinct because the customer can benefit from it on its own and it is separately identifiable: the licence works without updates, support is seen separately, and installation can be done by other installers, so there are four performance obligations. Option A treats the bundle as one item even though the parts are not dependent on each other. Option C leaves out installation, but the fact that approved installers elsewhere can do it shows it is a distinct service, and option B also leaves out the updates.

questions.question: ABC Limited enters into a contract with XYZ to sell its product for N200 per unit for the year 01.01.17 - 31.12.17. If XYZ purchases more than 1,200 units in the year, the price will decrease to N150 per unit (for all units). At the start of the contract ABC Limited did not expect XYZ to purchase more than 1,200 units. On 30.06.17, XYZ bought 600 units and another 500 units on 01.10.17, after which ABC Limited believed XYZ would meet the target. XYZ then bought a further 200 units on 1 December 2017. What is the total revenue ABC Limited should recognise from XYZ for the year ended 31.12.17?
questions.explanation: Once the 1,200-unit target is expected to be met, all units are priced at N150, so total revenue is 1,300 units x N150 = N195,000 (N120,000 + N75,000 + N30,000 - N30,000 adjustment on the first 600 units). Option A prices all 1,300 units at N200 and ignores the volume discount. Option B forgets to reduce the first 600 units from N200 to N150, and option C only counts 1,200 units.

questions.question: ABC Limited enters into a contract with XYZ to sell its product for N200 per unit for the year 01.01.17 - 31.12.17. If XYZ purchases more than 1,200 units in the year, the price will decrease to N150 per unit (for all units). At the start of the contract ABC Limited did not expect XYZ to purchase more than 1,200 units. On 30.06.17, XYZ bought 600 units and another 500 units on 01.10.17, after which ABC Limited believed XYZ would meet the target. XYZ then bought a further 200 units on 1 December 2017. When ABC Limited revises its expectation on 01.10.17, what adjustment must it make to the revenue already recognised on the first 600 units?
questions.explanation: The first 600 units were recorded at N200 each (N120,000), but once the discount is expected to apply they are worth only N150 each (N90,000), so revenue is reduced by 600 x N50 = N30,000 (Dr Revenue, Cr Trade receivables). Option B moves revenue in the wrong direction. Option C applies the N50 difference to the 500 units of the second sale instead, and option D ignores that variable consideration must be updated when expectations change.

questions.question: A software company sells a bundle that includes both a software license and a 12-month support service for a total price of N1,200,000. If sold separately, the software license would cost N1,000,000 and the support service N300,000. How would you allocate the transaction price (to the nearest naira)?

options.a: Software license N1,000,000; support service N200,000
options.b: Software license N923,077; support service N276,923
options.c: Software license N900,000; support service N300,000
options.d: Software license N600,000; support service N600,000

questions.explanation: The price is allocated in proportion to stand-alone selling prices: total N1,300,000, so the licence gets N1,000,000 / N1,300,000 x N1,200,000 = N923,077 and support gets N300,000 / N1,300,000 x N1,200,000 = N276,923. Option A puts the whole N100,000 discount on the support service, and option C puts it all on the licence, but a bundle discount is shared across all obligations unless there is evidence it belongs to one. Option D simply splits the price equally.

questions.question: A retailer sells a customer a package consisting of a computer and a printer for N700,000. The retailer realises that there are two separate performance obligations involved. It regularly sells the computer for N500,000 and the printer for N300,000. How will the retailer allocate the total transaction price between the computer and the printer?
questions.explanation: Stand-alone prices total N800,000, so the computer gets N500,000 / N800,000 x N700,000 = N437,500 and the printer gets N300,000 / N800,000 x N700,000 = N262,500, sharing the N100,000 discount in proportion. Options B and C load the whole discount onto one item, which IFRS 15 does not allow without evidence that the discount relates only to that item. Option D splits the price equally and ignores the stand-alone prices.

questions.question: The objective of IFRS 15 is to report useful information about certain features of revenue and cash flows arising from a contract with a customer. Which of the following is NOT one of those features?
questions.explanation: IFRS 15 aims to give users useful information about the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows from contracts with customers. Profitability is not on that list, because the standard is about how and when revenue is reported, not how much profit is made. Options A, C and D are all genuine parts of the objective.

questions.question: By setting principles for reporting revenue from contracts with customers, IFRS 15 aims to promote which of the following?

options.a: Higher reported profits for entities in all industries
options.b: Faster collection of trade receivables from customers
options.c: Uniform selling prices across competing entities
options.d: Consistency and comparability across industries and capital markets

questions.explanation: IFRS 15 sets one set of principles for revenue so that entities in different industries and capital markets report revenue in a consistent and comparable way. Option A is wrong because the standard does not aim to raise profits; it aims to report them faithfully. Options B and C are business outcomes that an accounting standard does not try to control.

questions.question: In IFRS 15, a customer is a party that has contracted with an entity to obtain goods or services that are

options.a: an output of the entity's ordinary activities in exchange for consideration
options.b: any asset of the entity, including its old property, plant and equipment
options.c: a contribution from the entity's equity participants
options.d: supplied free of charge as part of the entity's social responsibility

questions.explanation: A customer contracts to obtain goods or services that are an output of the entity's ordinary activities, in exchange for consideration. Option B is wrong because buying an entity's old equipment is not buying its ordinary output. Option C describes owners, not customers, and option D is wrong because a customer gives consideration in exchange.

questions.question: Income arising in the course of an entity's ordinary activities is called
questions.explanation: Revenue is income that arises in the course of an entity's ordinary activities, such as a supermarket selling groceries. Option B, equity, is the owners' residual interest, not a type of income. Option C is what a customer pays or promises in exchange for goods or services, and option D is a promise to transfer a distinct good or service.

questions.question: Income is defined as increases in economic benefits during the accounting period that increase equity. Which of the following is specifically excluded from income?

options.a: Inflows of assets from the sale of goods
options.c: Decreases of liabilities that increase equity
options.d: Enhancements of assets that increase equity

questions.explanation: Income covers inflows or enhancements of assets and decreases of liabilities that increase equity, other than those relating to contributions from equity participants. Money put in by owners increases equity but is not income. Options A, C and D are all forms of income named in the definition.

questions.question: Adaeze Foods Ltd, a Lagos supermarket chain, had the following inflows in a year. Which one is revenue under IFRS 15?

options.a: Cash paid in by the owners to expand the business
options.b: A long-term loan received from a commercial bank
options.c: New shares issued to existing shareholders for cash

questions.explanation: Revenue is income that arises from an entity's ordinary activities, and selling groceries is exactly what a supermarket does. Options A and C are contributions from equity participants, which are excluded from income altogether. Option B is a loan, which creates a liability rather than an increase in equity.

questions.question: CleanPro Ltd contracts to clean a Victoria Island office every day for one year. Each day's cleaning is distinct, substantially the same as other days, and transferred in the same pattern. How is this promise best described under IFRS 15?

options.a: No performance obligation until the year ends
options.b: A contribution from the customer to the entity's equity
options.c: 365 separate contracts with the same customer
options.d: A single performance obligation made up of a series of distinct services

questions.explanation: A performance obligation can be a series of distinct goods or services that are substantially the same and have the same pattern of transfer, which fits daily cleaning over a year. Option C is wrong because there is one agreement creating enforceable rights and obligations, not 365 contracts. Option A is wrong because the promise exists from contract inception, and option B confuses a customer with an owner.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the five steps in the IFRS 15 revenue model?

options.a: Identify the contract; determine the transaction price; identify the performance obligations; recognise revenue; allocate the transaction price
options.b: Identify the contract; identify the performance obligations; determine the transaction price; allocate the transaction price; recognise revenue
options.c: Identify the performance obligations; identify the contract; allocate the transaction price; determine the transaction price; recognise revenue
options.d: Determine the transaction price; identify the contract; identify the performance obligations; allocate the transaction price; recognise revenue

questions.explanation: The model starts with the contract, then the promises in it, then the price, then splits that price across the promises, and finally recognises revenue as each promise is satisfied. Option C wrongly puts performance obligations before the contract and allocation before the price is known. Option A recognises revenue before the price has been allocated, and option D prices a contract before identifying it.

questions.question: Step 3 of the IFRS 15 five-step model is to

options.b: recognise revenue when a performance obligation is satisfied
options.d: identify the performance obligations in the contract

questions.explanation: Step 3 is determining the transaction price, the amount of consideration the entity expects to be entitled to. Option C is Step 4, which comes only after the price is known. Option D is Step 2 and option B is Step 5.

questions.question: Distributing the transaction price to the identified performance obligations based on the stand-alone selling price of each distinct good or service is which step of the IFRS 15 model?
questions.explanation: Step 4 is the allocation of the transaction price across the performance obligations using their relative stand-alone selling prices. Option D, Step 2, only identifies the performance obligations. Option B, Step 3, works out the total price before it is shared out, and option A, Step 5, is when revenue is recognised.

questions.question: Checking whether an agreement has commercial substance and whether its payment terms can be identified is carried out at which step of the IFRS 15 model?

options.a: Step 5 - Recognise revenue when a performance obligation is satisfied
options.c: Step 1 - Identify the contract with the customer

questions.explanation: Commercial substance and identifiable payment terms are among the criteria that must all be met for a contract to exist, which is the test in Step 1. Option B looks at the distinct promises inside a contract that already exists. Options A and D come later, once a valid contract and its price are known.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the form of a contract under IFRS 15 is correct?

options.a: A contract covers only goods or services explicitly listed in the written agreement
options.b: A contract may be written, non-written or implied by the entity's customary business practices
options.c: A contract exists only after the customer has paid in full
options.d: A contract exists only if it is written and signed by both parties

questions.explanation: A contract can be written, non-written or implied, and it may include goods or services the customer expects because of the entity's business practices or statements. Option D is wrong because an oral or implied agreement can also create enforceable rights. Option A ignores implied promises, and option C confuses the existence of a contract with payment.

questions.question: PhoneHub Ltd, an Ikeja phone retailer, has always fitted a free screen protector for every customer who buys a phone, although its sales receipt does not mention this. How should the fitting be viewed under IFRS 15?

options.a: As outside the contract, because it is not written on the receipt
options.b: As a contribution from PhoneHub's equity participants
options.c: As income that is not revenue, because it is free
options.d: As a promise in the contract, because customers expect it from the entity's customary business practice

questions.explanation: Contracts are not limited to goods or services explicitly written down; they also include those the customer expects because of the entity's business practices. Option A is wrong for exactly that reason. Option B misuses the equity-participants idea, and option C is wrong because the fitting is part of what the customer pays for when buying the phone.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the criteria that must be met for a contract with a customer to fall within the scope of IFRS 15?

options.b: The customer has obtained legal title to the asset
options.c: The contract has been approved by parties committed to performing their obligations
options.d: The payment terms of the contract have been identified

questions.explanation: Legal title is an indicator, used in Step 5, that control of an asset has passed to the customer; it is not a condition for a contract to exist. Options A, C and D are all genuine Step 1 criteria, together with identifiable rights of each party and probable collection of the consideration.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the criteria for identifying a contract with a customer under IFRS 15?

options.a: The customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits
options.b: The rights of each party to the contract can be identified
options.c: The customer has physical possession of the asset
options.d: The stand-alone selling price of each good is observable

questions.explanation: For a contract to exist, the rights of each party must be identifiable, along with approval, identified payment terms, commercial substance and probable collection. Option A is a criterion for recognising revenue over time in Step 5. Option D relates to allocation in Step 4, and option C is an indicator that control has passed at a point in time.

questions.question: If an arrangement with a customer fails any of the five contract criteria in IFRS 15, which of the following is correct?

options.a: The arrangement is automatically cancelled and can never be revisited
options.b: The entity recognises revenue only for the criteria that were met
options.c: An accounting contract does not exist, even though a legal contract may exist
options.d: Revenue is recognised immediately because a legal contract exists

questions.explanation: All five criteria must be met; if any fails, there is no contract for IFRS 15 purposes even if the agreement is legally binding. Option D is wrong because legal enforceability alone is not enough. Option A is wrong because the entity keeps reassessing whether the criteria are later met, and option B is wrong because there is no partial contract.

questions.question: When a contract with a customer does not initially meet the IFRS 15 contract criteria, the entity should

options.a: recognise revenue on a straight-line basis over the contract term
options.b: derecognise the customer and stop assessing the arrangement
options.c: treat all amounts already received as income immediately
options.d: continue to assess the contract to determine whether the criteria are subsequently met

questions.explanation: If the criteria are not met at first, the entity must keep assessing the arrangement to see whether the criteria are met later. Option B is wrong because the assessment does not stop. Option A has no basis since there is no contract yet, and option C is wrong because amounts received are not simply income while the criteria remain unmet.

questions.question: Okon Plastics Ltd has made goods worth N15,000,000 exclusively for a customer that is undergoing restructuring because of liquidity problems. The customer promises a letter of credit from a bank, but it has not yet been finalised. Which contract criterion is in doubt?

options.a: The transaction price excludes amounts collected for third parties
options.b: It is probable that the entity will collect the consideration it is entitled to
options.d: The goods are distinct from other goods in the contract

questions.explanation: A contract exists only if it is probable that the entity will collect the consideration it is entitled to, and a customer with liquidity problems and no finalised letter of credit puts this in doubt. Option C is not the issue, since a genuine sale of goods has commercial substance. Option D is a Step 2 test, and option A concerns measuring the price in Step 3.

questions.question: A Lagos supplier receives a non-refundable deposit for 500 machines, but the price per machine has not been agreed because it depends on the cost of a part from another vendor. Which IFRS 15 contract criterion has NOT been met?

options.a: The contract has been approved by the parties
options.b: The rights of each party can be identified
options.c: The payment terms of the contract have been identified

questions.explanation: With no agreed price, the payment terms cannot be identified, so the contract criteria are not all met. Option D is not the problem, because selling machines for payment has commercial substance. Options A and B are not in doubt either, since both parties have agreed to the sale and know what each is to give and receive.

questions.question: Which of the following is a criterion for a good or service to be distinct under IFRS 15?

options.a: The customer has accepted the asset
options.b: The customer can benefit from it on its own or together with other readily available resources
options.c: Its stand-alone selling price is higher than its cost
options.d: The entity has a present right to payment for it

questions.explanation: A good or service is distinct if the customer can benefit from it alone or with readily available resources, and the promise is separately identifiable from other promises in the contract. Options A and D are indicators that control has passed at a point in time, used in Step 5. Option C is about profitability and has nothing to do with being distinct.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a consideration in deciding whether a promised good or service is distinct?

options.a: Whether the promise is separately identifiable from other promises in the contract
options.b: Whether the customer has legal title to the asset
options.c: Whether it is integrated with or dependent on other goods or services in the contract
options.d: Whether the customer can benefit from it on its own or with readily available resources

questions.explanation: Legal title is an indicator of transfer of control at a point in time, which belongs to Step 5. Options A, C and D are exactly the tests for distinctness: benefit on its own or with readily available resources, separately identifiable, and not integrated with or dependent on other promised items.

questions.question: A software vendor sells a licence with installation. Which fact best shows that the installation service is distinct from the licence?

options.a: The installation is priced within the same contract as the licence
options.b: The licence is for a standard software product
options.c: The vendor issues one invoice for both items
options.d: The installation is also carried out by several approved third-party installers

questions.explanation: If other installers can perform the installation, the customer can benefit from the licence together with readily available resources, so installation is not integrated with or dependent on the licence. Option B relates to the licence, not the service. Options A and C only show the items are sold together, which does not stop them being distinct.

questions.question: The transaction price under IFRS 15 is the amount of consideration to which an entity expects to be entitled in exchange for transferring promised goods or services, excluding

options.a: any discounts and rebates granted to the customer
options.b: amounts that depend on a future event
options.c: the cost of the goods or services transferred
options.d: amounts collected on behalf of third parties, such as some sales taxes

questions.explanation: The transaction price excludes amounts collected on behalf of third parties, such as VAT collected for the tax authority. Option A is wrong because discounts and rebates are factored into the price rather than excluded as third-party amounts. Option B describes variable consideration, which is also included in the estimate, and option C is wrong because cost is not part of the price at all.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a determinant of the transaction price under IFRS 15?

options.c: The entity's cost of producing the goods
options.d: Returns, discounts, rebates and other variable consideration

questions.explanation: The transaction price is what the entity expects to be entitled to from the customer, so production cost does not determine it. Options A, B and D are all determinants: the contract terms, customary business practices, and factors such as returns, bonuses, discounts, rebates and variable consideration.

questions.question: When an entity's entitlement to consideration depends on the occurrence or non-occurrence of a future event, such as a volume target or performance bonus, the consideration is described as
questions.explanation: Consideration that can change depending on whether a future event happens, such as a volume discount or bonus, is variable consideration. Option A is the price at which an item would be sold separately. Option B relates to the time value of money when payment timing gives a significant financing benefit, and option C describes owners' contributions.
